applianceModels.name: French Door Bottom-Freezer (Samsung, LG, Whirlpool, GE)
applianceModels.airflowMechanism: Freezer bottom evaporator with motorized damper duct to upper fresh food cabin
applianceModels.defrostType: Electronic Control Board with NTC Thermistor & Bi-Metal Thermal Fuse
applianceModels.failureVulnerability: High risk of iced evaporator drain pan and stepper motor damper freeze-up, causing upper compartment to climb to 50°F+ while freezer appears frozen.

applianceModels.name: Traditional Top-Mount Freezer (Frigidaire, Whirlpool, Kenmore)
applianceModels.airflowMechanism: Freezer back panel evaporator coil with manual slide air diffuser into lower cabin
applianceModels.defrostType: Mechanical Defrost Timer (8-hr / 10-hr) + Clip-On Bi-Metal Thermostat (L45-20F)
applianceModels.failureVulnerability: Bi-metal thermostat dome swells and leaks moisture, preventing defrost heater activation. Evaporator turns into solid block of ice within 96 hours.

applianceModels.name: Side-by-Side Refrigerator-Freezer (KitchenAid, GE Profile, Bosch)
applianceModels.airflowMechanism: Vertical freezer tower fan exhausting through return and supply ports along divider wall
applianceModels.defrostType: Adaptive Defrost Control (ADC) with defrost terminator thermostat
applianceModels.failureVulnerability: Divider wall return air tunnel prone to ice occlusion. Door gasket sag introduces humid ambient air, accelerating frost choking.

applianceModels.name: Compact Mini Fridge / Dorm Refrigerator with Freezer Box
applianceModels.airflowMechanism: Convection cooling from internal cold plate box with no fan motor
applianceModels.failureVulnerability: No active heater; severe rime ice build-up insulates the cold plate, causing temperature to rise above 45°F without consumer awareness.

applianceModels.name: Commercial Reach-In Stainless Cooler (True, Turbo Air, Beverage-Air)
applianceModels.airflowMechanism: High-CFM ceiling evaporator coil with timed fan-delay defrost cycle
applianceModels.defrostType: Digital Dixell / Carel Controller with Off-Cycle or Electric Defrost Rods
applianceModels.failureVulnerability: Constant kitchen line door openings overload evaporator fins with kitchen grease and steam, triggering rapid coil icing.

failureModes.name: Bi-Metal Defrost Thermostat Open-Circuit (Coils Frozen Solid)
failureModes.electricalBehavior: Thermostat contacts stay permanently open (infinite Ohms / OL). Defrost heater never energizes.
failureModes.tempTrajectory: Freezer remains 15°F–24°F initially, but evaporator coils freeze into a solid block of ice. Air passages close completely within 3–5 days, and fresh food section warms to 48°F–58°F.
failureModes.visualSign: Freezer back metal panel frosted over; fan running but no cool air blowing from refrigerator vents.

failureModes.name: Thermostat Contacts Welded Closed / Heater Runaway
failureModes.electricalBehavior: Thermostat fails to trip at 45°F–50°F; heater continues to draw 500W during entire defrost window or sticks on.
failureModes.tempTrajectory: Freezer temperature spikes dramatically to 50°F–65°F during defrost; interior plastic liner melts or warps; refrigerator temperature rises rapidly to 52°F+.
failureModes.visualSign: Burning plastic smell, melting ice cubes turning into puddles in freezer, warm radiant heat felt on freezer back panel.

failureModes.name: Defrost Timer Motor Stalled in Defrost Mode
failureModes.electricalBehavior: Timer cam ceases rotation while contacts are switched to the heater circuit. Compressor and evaporator fan never restart.
failureModes.tempTrajectory: Entire appliance powers down cooling completely. Both freezer and refrigerator warm toward room temperature (68°F–75°F) within 8–16 hours.
failureModes.visualSign: Complete appliance silence; interior bulb illuminates when door opens, but zero compressor humming or fan vibration.

failureModes.name: Evaporator Fan Motor Bearing Seizure or Blade Ice-Strike
failureModes.electricalBehavior: Fan motor winding energized (warm to touch) but rotor locked by ice formation or worn sleeve bearings.
failureModes.tempTrajectory: Freezer remains cold (0°F–10°F) via localized static heat exchange, but zero cold air is pushed into the refrigerator compartment, which rises to 54°F–62°F.
failureModes.visualSign: Chirping, groaning, or grinding sound from freezer panel followed by sudden silence; no air velocity felt at fresh food air baffle.

failureModes.name: Defrost Condensate Drain Hole Frozen / Clogged with Slime
failureModes.electricalBehavior: Electrical defrost circuit works normally, but melted water cannot drain to compressor evaporation pan.
failureModes.tempTrajectory: Compartment temperature stays near 38°F–42°F, but 100% relative humidity causes heavy condensation dripping on food items, accelerating bacterial biofilm and mold growth.
failureModes.visualSign: Thick sheet of ice frozen on the bottom floor of the freezer or water pooling under the fresh food vegetable crisper drawers.

pathogens.name: Listeria monocytogenes
pathogens.clinicalSeverity: Severe: 20–30% mortality in high-risk groups. Causes meningitis, septicemia, spontaneous miscarriage, and stillbirth in pregnant individuals.

pathogens.name: Salmonella enterica
pathogens.clinicalSeverity: High: Acute salmonellosis with severe abdominal cramping, fever, diarrhea, and potential reactive arthritis or systemic bacteremia.

pathogens.name: Staphylococcus aureus (Enterotoxin Producers)
pathogens.doublingTimeAt55F: Rapid log phase; heat-stable enterotoxin A/B synthesized within 4–6 hours
pathogens.clinicalSeverity: Violent Acute Toxicity: Toxin is heat-stable and survives boiling for 30 minutes. Causes sudden projectile vomiting and severe cramps within 1–6 hours of ingestion.

pathogens.name: Bacillus cereus (Emetic & Diarrheal)
pathogens.clinicalSeverity: Emetic Cereulide Toxin: Extremely heat-stable ring peptide preformed in starches; not inactivated by standard reheating (resists 121°C for 90 min).

foodTriageList.items: Raw Chicken Breast, Thighs, Ground Turkey, Ground Beef
foodTriageList.rationale: High surface moisture and nutrient broth allow Salmonella and Campylobacter to enter exponential multiplication. Never cook spoiled poultry to 'sterilize' it.

foodTriageList.items: Whole Milk, 2% Milk, Skim Milk, Heavy Cream
foodTriageList.verdictAt4HoursAt48F: SMELL & SOUR TEST / DISCARD IF >45°F OVER 3 HRS
foodTriageList.rationale: Lactococcus and psychrotrophic Pseudomonas multiply, fermenting lactose into lactic acid causing curdling, bitter peptides, and off-flavors.

foodTriageList.items: Brie, Camembert, Ricotta, Fresh Mozzarella, Queso Fresco, Feta
foodTriageList.rationale: High water activity (aw > 0.95) and near-neutral pH create the ultimate incubation vector for Listeria monocytogenes.

foodTriageList.items: Cheddar, Parmesan, Pecorino, Swiss, Gouda, Provolone
foodTriageList.rationale: Low water activity (aw < 0.85) and high salt content physically prevent enteric bacterial proliferation even if oil sweats onto surface.

foodTriageList.items: Grade A Large Washed Eggs in Shell
foodTriageList.verdictAt4HoursAt48F: COOK THOROUGHLY (>165°F) IMMEDIATELY; DO NOT USE RAW
foodTriageList.rationale: Washed US/Canadian eggs lack protective cuticle. Condensation on shells from warming allows surface bacteria to be pulled through shell pores via negative pressure.

foodTriageList.items: Fried Rice, Cooked Penne, Lasagna, Stews, Soups
foodTriageList.rationale: Bacillus cereus endospores survive cooking and germinate in warm starches, rapidly releasing the vomiting-inducing cereulide enterotoxin.

foodTriageList.items: Ketchup, Yellow Mustard, Commercial Mayonnaise, Pickles, Jam
foodTriageList.rationale: High titratable acidity (pH < 4.0) with acetic or citric acid, coupled with low water activity, prevents pathogenic bacterial proliferation.

foodTriageList.items: Prepared Powdered Formula, Thawed Expressed Breast Milk
foodTriageList.rationale: Extreme vulnerability of neonatal immune systems. Cronobacter sakazakii and Listeria can cause fatal necrotizing enterocolitis or infant sepsis.

multimeterDiagnosticGuide.location: Clipped directly to the top or side metal tube of the freezer evaporator coil.
multimeterDiagnosticGuide.testCondition: Must be tested while frosty/cold (<20°F / -6°C). If fridge is already warm, submerge in ice water bath for 5 minutes.
multimeterDiagnosticGuide.failureIndication: Infinite Resistance (O.L. or open circuit) while cold means thermostat is blown and will never trigger the defrost heater.

multimeterDiagnosticGuide.location: Located directly along the bottom perimeter or woven underneath the evaporator coil.
multimeterDiagnosticGuide.testCondition: Disconnect both wiring spade terminals before testing.
multimeterDiagnosticGuide.failureIndication: O.L. / Open circuit indicates the calrod internal wire has burned open and element must be replaced.

multimeterDiagnosticGuide.location: Inside fresh food control console or in lower compressor compartment at rear.
multimeterDiagnosticGuide.testCondition: Locate manual advance screw notch. Turn clockwise with flat screwdriver until loud click is heard.
multimeterDiagnosticGuide.expectedReading: Compressor stops instantly and heater energizes. Motor should resume turning cam and advance out within 25–35 minutes.
multimeterDiagnosticGuide.failureIndication: If compressor never restarts on its own after 45 minutes, timer motor gear is stripped or winding burned out.

multimeterDiagnosticGuide.location: Mounted on steel bracket centered above evaporator coil in freezer back wall.
multimeterDiagnosticGuide.testCondition: Check voltage at fan harness while door switch is depressed (120V AC on older models, 12V DC on inverter models).
multimeterDiagnosticGuide.expectedReading: 1.5K to 3K Ohms on coil winding; shaft spins freely with finger flick.
multimeterDiagnosticGuide.failureIndication: Shaft feels stiff, gummy, or locked; winding reads O.L. indicates burned motor.
